messages.text: ok wall staring done. back. that one-pager by friday is tight but doable. mostly just need to list what we actually process vs what we cache, right?

heads up: keep it high level for the chair. no code snippets or tensor shapes. just 'data stays on campus hardware, models run locally, no third-party API calls'. and emphasize the double opt-in messaging.
got it. 'local hardware' is technically true (the GX10 box) but it sounds like a server farm if i say it wrong. i'll phrase it as 'department-owned compute'.
yes, that's better. also, we're thinking of starting with just one course for the pilot. maybe CS 310 or something similar? about 60 students.
60 is a good size. not so small it's noise, not so big we break the rate limits on my retry logic. which course are you leaning toward?
leaning toward CS 431 actually. you're in that one, right? Nina and Amara's group is doing the Raft thing. feels natural to test the 'who knows about distributed systems' angle there.

haha, testing it on myself and my teammates. bias alert. but honestly, we have a lot of diverse interests in that group so the graph should look decent. i can seed the test data from our actual course profile if you want a dry run before the 29th.
that would be perfect. send me a link to the sandbox or a static export of the 'why you connect' explanations for your group. i'll share it with the chair so she sees the quality before the meeting.
on it. i'll pull the explanations for John/Nina/Amara and maybe add one or two other students from the course to make it look less like a clique. give me till tomorrow morning.
sounds good. thanks for moving fast on this, john. it really does help that you can show the 'why' immediately without needing a cloud backend spin-up time.
